policy.primaryDomain: The mainUrl in each provider Kotlin file is authoritative and is updated only after verification.
discovery: HTTP redirects issued by the provider's currently configured domain
cross-domain canonical or og:url metadata from the currently configured domain
candidateDomains explicitly registered by the maintainer
links found on explicitly trusted discoveryUrls registered by the maintainer
last-resort search-engine results used only as untrusted candidate nominations
policy.verification: A candidate must return a substantial HTML page and match the saved identityProfile or every configured identityMarker. Search results only nominate candidates and never authorize a change by themselves. A successful HTTP response alone is never enough.
safety: Search results are untrusted candidates; lookalike, parked, placeholder, and protection pages are rejected.
403, 429, Cloudflare challenges, and transient timeouts are not proof of a domain change.
A candidate is not automatically applied if site identity cannot be verified.
If the old domain is fully offline, search can nominate possible domains but cannot authorize a switch without a saved identity profile or explicit identityMarkers.
policy.onSwitch: Only the affected provider module is changed, its mainUrl and same-provider host references are updated, and its plugin version is incremented. The normal CloudStream build is then dispatched.
policy.switchRule: A provider domain may be changed only after two independent checks confirm HTTP 404/410, a persistent parked-domain page, permanent DNS-not-found, connection-refused, or a TLS hostname/common-name mismatch. Any 2xx/3xx response, including a redirect to another hostname, means the current URL is working and must be retained. 401/403/429/451, Cloudflare challenges, generic TLS issuer/expiry errors, 5xx responses and timeouts never trigger a switch.
limits: Working 2xx/3xx primary domains are immutable to the automatic updater, including domains that redirect.
A confirmed failure must be observed twice before candidate discovery starts.
403/429/Cloudflare protection, generic TLS issuer/expiry errors, timeouts and 5xx responses are not proof that a domain changed.
A TLS hostname/common-name mismatch is a domain failure only after two independent confirmations.
A replacement must pass identity verification after the primary domain is confirmed dead.
policy.workingDomainRule: Never rewrite a provider's current domain when it responds successfully or redirects successfully. Only confirmed dead primary domains may enter candidate discovery.
